text: So incredible that he could not believe it.
General Sheridan, July eighteen seventy six. He read in the morning paper that Custer was dead. How did the paper know first?
Custer killed. Every man killed. Three hundred and fifteen.
The source: a civilian scout, who rode to the telegraph in Bozeman, Montana.
General Sherman: it must be exaggerated.
Mid-interview, there's a rap at the door. Custer's death is confirmed.
The army's own dispatch, coming by steamboat, confirmed the newspaper reports.
The count was too high. Two hundred and sixty eight died. But the general? He read it in the paper.
